record.title: Nigeria Tsamiya Kamba corridor continued restrictions and 2026 reopening
record.direction: Benin via Nigeria to Niger for the retained transit-truck phase.
record.movement: For the retained February 2026 phase: Cotonou-origin transit goods trucks destined for Niger; passenger restriction not established by this phase.
record.imposing_authority: Closure authority disputed between Nigeria and Niger in contemporary reports; Nigeria Customs authorised the 9 February 2026 transit reopening.
record.enforcement: Contemporary Presidency statement reports resumed commerce; independently published ISS commentary describes truck movement. Full crossing-level phase history unresolved.
record.relationship: Nested implementation history of W-001 and W-015; not an additional independent national closure decision.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.context: ISS describes restored corridor traffic in February 2026. Contemporary Tribune reporting separates Tsamiya permission from February 9 Kamba reopening. An April 2022 customs circular had already approved Kamba reopening, so this is a nested, phased implementation history rather than a single continuous 2019–2026 shutdown.
record.uncertainty: Recent Cotonou-to-Niger truck restriction reportedly lasted months before February 9, 2026 restoration. Banouto attributes it to Niger authorities; Anadolu and Nigerian local reports attribute it to Nigeria and quote Nigerian reopening orders. Exact onset and authority attribution remain unresolved. This is distinct from the 2019 regime and 2022 Kamba permission.
